extracted.intended_audience: readers of national/international news (general public, policymakers, diplomats)
extracted.subtask_description: An AP-style news report summarizing decisions and statements from the Moscow foreign ministers' conference and related post‑war administrative arrangements for Japan, Korea, Europe and atomic-energy controls. Geared toward readers wanting authoritative summaries of international agreements and their practical implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Far Eastern Commission voting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: This Far Eastern commission will act by a majority vote which, however, must include the concurring votes of Great Britain, the Soviet Union, China and the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions must have a majority but are only valid if the four principal powers concur; the Article explains this requirement and its effect on basic Allied policy for Japan.

rubrics_metrics.name: 11‑nation commission veto/reserved powers
rubrics_metrics.description: An 11‑nation commission in Washington, with the veto power reserved for the U. S., Russia, Britain and China, assured that no basic Allied policy for Japan could be adopted without American concurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The arrangement reserves final blocking power to four principal states so that no 'basic Allied policy' on Japan can be adopted without concurrence of these major powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. authority to issue interim directives to the Supreme Commander
rubrics_metrics.description: The provision for the U. S. to issue interim directives to MacArthur 'on all urgent matters'—pending agreement in the Far Eastern commission the U.S. is free to give interim directives on all urgent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives the U.S. temporary directive power over urgent administrative matters in Japan until the commission reaches agreement; the article stresses this safeguards 'efficient administration' under the Supreme Commander.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three reserved questions requiring commission approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Only three subjects were excepted from the U.S. interim power and require commission approval: 1. Changes in the control of Japan as set forth in the surrender terms; 2. Fundamental changes in the Japanese constitutional structure; 3. Changes in the Japanese government as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three matters are explicitly carved out as requiring collective Allied/commission action rather than unilateral interim directives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allied council for Japan: composition and advisory role
rubrics_metrics.description: An Allied council for Japan to be composed of representatives of the Soviet Union, the British commonwealth, China and the United States under the chairmanship of General MacArthur; the council is to advise and consult with the supreme commander in carrying out the terms of surrender.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The council is advisory; the Supreme Commander's decision will be controlling except on the three reserved questions. The article explains the council's role is consultative, not to supplant administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supreme Commander retention of administrative authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposals... assure that the authority of Gen. MacArthur will not be obstructed... General MacArthur will not be obstructed by the inability of the Far Eastern commission to agree on policies or by the inability of the Allied council to agree upon the methods of carrying them out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinforces that day‑to‑day administration remains with the Supreme Commander and that inability of multilateral bodies to agree should not block necessary administrative actions (subject to the three reserved matters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission decisions incorporated into directives to the Supreme Commander
rubrics_metrics.description: The decisions of the commission will be incorporated into directives to the Supreme Commander by the United States government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the commission reaches agreement, its decisions are to be transmitted as directives (via the U.S. government) to the Supreme Commander for implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atomic‑energy commission scope and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission powers will consist of making inquiries and recommendations but no government will be bound to act on those suggestions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The atomic‑energy matter is limited to inquiry/recommendation—no binding authority is ceded; technical/scientific details were not discussed in Moscow, per the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atomic safeguards and non‑sharing of armament secrets
rubrics_metrics.description: The matter of safeguards will apply to commission recommendations 'in relation to every phase of the subject and at every stage,' and neither the U. S. nor any other Nation would be expected to share its armament secrets until it was certain that 'effective safeguards had been developed to insure our mutual protection.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any international handling of atomic information is conditioned on development of effective safeguards; until then, nations will not be expected to divulge weapons 'know‑how.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and composition for postwar European peace conference
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreement under which a 21‑nation peace conference will be called not later than May 1, 1946... principal powers will draft treaties which will be submitted to the peace conference; all states which actively waged war with substantial military force against the European members of the Axis will be invited to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treaty drafting is first done by principal powers (signers of armistices) then reviewed by a broader peace conference which can make recommendations; final treaties require agreement of the relevant states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition conditions for Romania and Bulgaria
rubrics_metrics.description: The British and American governments will recognize the Romanian government as soon as they are satisfied that the government has been broadened to include two truly representative members of two important political parties not now represented... and assurances have been given regarding free elections, freedom of speech, press, religion, and association.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition is contingent on demonstrable broadening of representation and concrete assurances on civil liberties and free elections; similar steps are urged for Bulgaria with specified advisory/monitoring measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Korean provisional government and four‑power trusteeship plan
rubrics_metrics.description: They will make recommendations... for the formation of a Korean provisional democratic government. They will also make proposals to these governments regarding a four‑power trusteeship to prepare Korea for its independence within five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agreed plan contemplates a provisional government and consideration of a trusteeship period 'up to five years' to prepare Korea for independent nationhood; joint commissions will advise and propose administrative/economic measures.
